composers_checked.name: Legrenzi, Giovanni
composers_checked.note: 13 candidate pages (Opp. 2, 4, 8, La cetra and single pages). Kept 17 of Op. 2 (No. 16 is by his father, Giovanni Maria), 6 sonatas + the dances of Op. 4, 14 of Op. 8, 16 of La cetra; added Op. 16 (gap). Op. 18 is lost; the other opus numbers are vocal.

composers_checked.name: Marino, Carlo Antonio
composers_checked.note: Gap check (it.wikipedia list: Opp. 1-3, 7, 8): the Apple Music composer searches found only the two Tactus albums, so Op. 1 (sonate da camera a tre, 1687) and Op. 7 (sonate a tre, 1704) have no recording and IMSLP has no other in-scope page. The 'Concerto a 4' on Tactus (2012) has no score source found; not added

composers_checked.name: Avison, Charles
composers_checked.note: Gap check (Wikipedia list): his chamber works are Opp. 1, 5, 7, 8, all kept; the concertos (Opp. 2–4, 6, 9, 10, after Scarlatti and Geminiani) are string-orchestra concerti grossi and stay out

note: La cetra is cited as Op. 10 (Bonta's Harvard edition, recordings, Wikipedia); IMSLP files it as Op. 11 (the print's Op. 10 duplicates Acclamationi divote), so the IMSLP numbers are in aka. Legrenzi's violone / 'viola da brazzo' (bass violin) parts with their own line are counted as a cello part beside the continuo; the census folded some into the continuo. L'Obizza (Op. 8 No. 4) is listed on IMSLP for 2 violins and viola, but Clematis and the Mvsica Perdvta booklet give it as a sonata a 2 for violin and bass violin: entered as the latter. La Crispa: IMSLP and the Sonatori list 2 violins and violone, Mvsica Perdvta a violin and bass violin; entered as a 3. Avison Opp. 5, 7, 8: one reviewer (Op. 8) calls the string parts ad lib.; the prints say 'with accompaniments' and the recordings use them, so they are counted as parts. Op. 4 sonatas: Nos. 1–6 (da chiesa) counted with a separate violone, Nos. 7–12 and the dances with the bass as continuo (as in Seay's two editions). Floors for Op. 4 Nos. 1 and 4 and Op. 8 Nos. 3 and 6 rest partly on the Wikipedia discography (label and catalogue numbers given), not on a track list I opened. BY HAND (orchestrating session, 2026-10-17): the `notes` of the 18 Avison accompanied sonatas (Opp. 5, 7, 8) now start with "Strings ad lib. in the first edition" as brief change 3 requires; nothing else changed.
